s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive painful swelling and infiltration of the face, hands, and other areas with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Painful swelling of the face, particularly affecting the eyelids, periorbital tissues, and hands
Striking infiltration of the eyelids and periorbital skin with multiple firm tumorous swellings
Diffusely rippled appearance of the skin on the forehead, neck, shoulders, and anterior chest
key_facts: Increasing drowsiness and weakness over 7 days
Swollen hands and fingers with scattered focal purpuric infarcts
Dermal oedema and scattered histiocytes on deep incisional biopsy
Widespread fibrinoid exudates within deeper tissues
Granulomatous inflammation with intense neutrophilic abscesses in subcutaneous fat

shortlist.label: Scleromyxedema
shortlist.why_kept: matches clinical presentation of progressive painful swelling and infiltration of the face and hands, with histological findings of dermal oedema and mucin deposition

shortlist.label: Panniculitis
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with the patient's symptoms of swollen hands and fingers with purpuric infarcts, and histological findings of granulomatous inflammation and neutrophilic abscesses in subcutaneous fat

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the patient's presentation of progressive swelling and infiltration, although the absence of eosinophilia makes this diagnosis less likely

shortlist.label: Lipodermatosclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: possible diagnosis given the patient's symptoms of swollen hands and fingers, although the presence of systemic symptoms and granulomatous inflammation makes this less likely

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the patient's presentation of systemic symptoms, granulomatous inflammation, and neutrophilic abscesses, although the absence of renal involvement and normal complement concentrations makes this diagnosis less likely

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of progressive painful swelling, particularly affecting the eyelids, periorbital tissues, and hands, along with the histopathological findings of dermal oedema, scattered histiocytes, and mucin deposition (as indicated by Hale's colloidal iron staining), are characteristic of Scleromyxedema.

rejected.label: Panniculitis
rejected.why: While panniculitis could explain some of the skin findings, it does not fully account for the mucin deposition or the specific pattern of swelling and systemic symptoms described.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
rejected.why: The absence of eosinophilia in the laboratory tests makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Lipodermatosclerosis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a different pattern of skin changes, often related to chronic venous insufficiency, which is not indicated in the vignette.

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: The normal chest radiograph and the lack of other specific findings typical for Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (such as upper respiratory tract or renal involvement) make this diagnosis less likely.
